scope: src/main.js lines 29050-30740 (+ confirmed cross-refs to lines 11344, 33848, 37150, 37584, 38833, 18808, src/data/weapons.js): operator/HUD theme config, weapon unlock gates, focus screen FX, kill beat, rain/snow, camera punch, run summary/stats, profile slots, health regen, sparks/particles, combat tempo, zone+math utils, graffiti/texture gen.

findings.title: applyHudTheme sets --hud-* CSS vars that nothing in the project reads (inert theming feature)
findings.description: applyHudTheme() writes --hud-primary/--hud-secondary/--hud-accent/--hud-bg/--hud-text on documentElement, and a setTimeout at load applies the 'classic' theme. Grep across index.html and all src shows ZERO consumers of var(--hud-primary) etc. The entire HUD_THEMES system (29303-29336: classic/cyber/blood/forest) is therefore inert — selecting a theme changes nothing on screen.
findings.fix: Either (low-risk visible win) wire the HUD CSS so it actually consumes these vars — e.g. point the live crosshair/hitmarker/ammo accent colors at var(--hud-accent, #ffd060) and the HUD panel backgrounds at var(--hud-bg) in the inline <style> in index.html / the HUD style block — then expose a theme selector; or delete the dead theming block. Wiring it makes 4 selectable palettes light up instantly.
findings.risk: If wired, must keep a fallback (var(--hud-accent,#ffd060)) so existing default look is unchanged when no theme set. Pure deletion is zero-risk but loses a near-finished feature.

findings.title: RUN_STATS per-weapon/per-enemy tracking is never populated; compileFullRunStats() returns empty breakdowns
findings.description: recordKillStat(), recordShotStat() and resetRunStats() (lines 29983/29996/30001) have NO callers anywhere (grep confirms only their definitions). The live reset path uses a DIFFERENT function _resetRunStats() at line 37584 which does NOT touch RUN_STATS. Consequently RUN_STATS.perWeapon / perEnemyType / perBuilding stay empty for the whole run, and compileFullRunStats() (29053) — itself uncalled — copies empty objects into stats.perWeapon/perEnemyType. This is a fully orphaned stats subsystem masquerading as live telemetry.
findings.evidence: grep recordKillStat => only 'function recordKillStat' (def). grep resetRunStats => only def at 30001; real reset is _resetRunStats() (37584) which sets P.kills/headshots etc. but never clears RUN_STATS. stats.perWeapon=Object.assign({},RUN_STATS.perWeapon) // always {}
findings.fix: Either delete RUN_STATS + recordKillStat/recordShotStat/resetRunStats/compileFullRunStats (29977-30091, 30001-30005) as dead; OR wire it: call recordShotStat(P.weaponIdx,hit) in the shoot/hit path, recordKillStat(...) where P.kills++ happens (e.g. near the cinematicKill call sites at 14490/21433/26448), and add RUN_STATS reset inside _resetRunStats() at 37584. Naming collision (resetRunStats vs _resetRunStats) is the trap.
findings.risk: Wiring adds per-shot bookkeeping in the hot fire path — keep it O(1) object writes (it is). Deletion risk near-zero. Watch the _resetRunStats vs resetRunStats name collision when refactoring.

findings.title: tickHealthRegen (passive out-of-combat HP regen) is never called; CONFIG.player.hpRegen/hpRegenDelay also unused
findings.description: tickHealthRegen(dt) implements slow passive regen (1.5 hp/s after 5s without damage) but has no caller (grep: only the definition). The only regen actually wired into the loop is tickSlideRegen (33848, called at 41664) which ONLY regens while sliding. So a player standing still out of combat never recovers HP. CONFIG.player.hpRegen:1.5 and hpRegenDelay:5.0 (29525-29526) are likewise read nowhere — the function hardcodes its own 5000ms / 1.5 instead of referencing CONFIG. This is a half-wired survivability feature and a constants-defined-but-ignored contradiction.
findings.evidence: function tickHealthRegen(dt){...P.hp=Math.min(P.maxHp,P.hp+dt*1.5);}  // grep tickHealthRegen => 1 (def only). grep CONFIG.player.hpRegen => no matches. Loop only calls tickSlideRegen at 41664.
findings.fix: If passive regen is intended, add `if(typeof tickHealthRegen==='function'&&G.started)tickHealthRegen(dt);` next to the tickSlideRegen call at line 41664, and have it read CONFIG.player.hpRegen / hpRegenDelay*1000 instead of the hardcoded 1.5/5000 so the two stay in sync. If not intended, delete tickHealthRegen (29881-29888) and the orphan CONFIG fields.
findings.risk: Enabling passive regen changes game balance/feel — confirm design intent before wiring (it makes the game noticeably easier). Pure deletion is safe.

findings.title: WEAPON_UNLOCK_GATES + isWeaponUnlocked is a dead second source of weapon-unlock truth that disagrees with the authoritative WEAPONS table
findings.description: WEAPON_UNLOCK_GATES hardcodes idx0=M4A1 removed, idx1/2 always, idx3..7 gated by building number, and isWeaponUnlocked(idx) gates on PROGRESS._maxBuildingCleared. But the authoritative playable-weapon source is src/data/weapons.js (PLAYABLE_WEAPON_INDICES derived from WEAPONS[i].removed/.playable). isWeaponUnlocked() has NO callers (grep confirms), so this gate table is inert — yet it encodes a parallel, easily-drifting unlock policy (e.g. it asserts M4 idx0 removed while isPlayableWeaponIdx(0) is used as 'playable' at main.js:18808). Classic duplicate-config that will silently rot.
findings.evidence: 0:{removed:true,name:'M4A1'} ... function isWeaponUnlocked(idx){...return (PROGRESS._maxBuildingCleared||0)>=gate.building;}  // grep isWeaponUnlocked => def only. Authoritative: weapons.js PLAYABLE_WEAPON_INDICES=WEAPONS.map(...!w.removed...).
findings.fix: Delete WEAPON_UNLOCK_GATES + isWeaponUnlocked, or derive the gate names/states from the WEAPONS table at runtime instead of a hand-maintained literal so it cannot disagree. If a real unlock-gate UI is desired, have isWeaponUnlocked delegate to isPlayableWeaponIdx for base playability.
findings.risk: None if deleted (dead). If kept and wired, ensure it doesn't override weapons.js gating — keep weapons.js authoritative.

findings.title: loadProfileSlot does Object.assign(PROGRESS, partial) — would clobber PROGRESS with a partial shape (violates save-merge rule); whole profile-slot system is dead
findings.description: loadProfileSlot(slot) does `Object.assign(PROGRESS, JSON.parse(raw))`, merging a stored slot directly onto the live PROGRESS object WITHOUT merging against defaults first. Per the project save-compatibility rule, persisted shapes must always be merged against defaults, never overwritten with a partial shape — and a slot saved by an older build (missing newer keys) would leave PROGRESS partially undefined after load. This is a latent save-corruption bug. It is currently masked because loadProfileSlot/saveProfileSlot/listProfileSlots all have ZERO callers (grep confirms) — the multi-profile feature is entirely unwired.
findings.fix: If the feature ships, route loads through the same defaults-merge used for clearance_progress (deep-merge JSON.parse(raw) onto a fresh defaults clone, then assign) rather than Object.assign onto live PROGRESS. If not shipping, delete loadProfileSlot/saveProfileSlot/listProfileSlots (29817-29837) to remove the footgun.
findings.risk: Save-compat: a naive merge could resurrect deleted keys; mirror the existing clearance_progress merge helper exactly. Deletion is zero-risk.

findings.title: cinematicKillEnhanced (boss/lieutenant kill flash + slow-mo) and _flashScreenColor are never called — boss kills get no extra punch
findings.description: cinematicKillEnhanced(hitPt,enemy) wraps the live cinematicKill() and adds type-specific flair: a gold full-screen flash + slow-mo on boss kills, red flash + slow-mo on lieutenant kills, and a streak flash on 10+ combos. But every kill site calls plain cinematicKill(...) (14490, 20166, 21433, 21505, 23128, 26448, 27667) — cinematicKillEnhanced has no callers. Its only consumer, _flashScreenColor (29659), is therefore also transitively dead. Result: boss/lieutenant kills lack the intended cinematic emphasis.
findings.evidence: function cinematicKillEnhanced(hitPt,enemy){cinematicKill(hitPt); if(enemy.isBoss){_flashScreenColor(0xffd060,800);triggerKillCamSlowMo(.20,2.5);} ...} // grep cinematicKillEnhanced => def only; all kill sites call cinematicKill(
findings.fix: At boss/lieutenant kill sites, swap cinematicKill(pos) for cinematicKillEnhanced(pos, enemy) (the kill paths already have the enemy object in scope, e.g. 14490/21433/26448). One-line swaps give an immediate, high-visibility gold flash + brief slow-mo on lieutenant/boss kills. Fix _flashScreenColor z-index note below before enabling.
findings.risk: triggerKillCamSlowMo on every boss/LT kill must not stack with an existing boss-death cinematic elsewhere — verify no double slow-mo. Low risk; visible payoff is large for boss moments.

findings.title: _flashScreenColor uses mix-blend-mode:screen at z-index:14 — likely under the HUD and dependent on backdrop; opacity .55 is harsh
findings.description: _flashScreenColor appends a full-screen div with mix-blend-mode:screen, opacity .55, z-index:14. mix-blend-mode:screen blends with whatever is BEHIND it in the same stacking context; a fixed overlay at z-index 14 may sit below HUD layers and its 'screen' blend can be effectively invisible over dark scenes or wash out over bright ones. If cinematicKillEnhanced is wired, this is the on-screen feedback, so it should be tuned to AAA standards.
findings.fix: Use a brief radial-vignette flash (background:radial-gradient(circle, transparent 35%, color 120%)) or a quick opacity .55->0 with mix-blend-mode:plus-lighter and a z-index just under the crosshair but above the world canvas, and shorten/keyframe the alpha (e.g. .45 -> 0 over 220ms) for a snappier hit feel. Keep pointer-events:none.
findings.risk: Cosmetic only; ensure z-index doesn't cover interactive HUD. No save/perf impact.

findings.title: _cameraPunch captures oldFov then restores via setTimeout — rapid repeat calls would permanently inflate FOV (latent; function is dead)
findings.description: _cameraPunch(amount) does oldFov=camera.fov; camera.fov+=amount*4; ...setTimeout(()=>camera.fov=oldFov,80). If called twice within 80ms, the second call captures the ALREADY-inflated fov as its 'oldFov', and the first timeout restores to the pre-first value while the second restores to the inflated value — net FOV creep. Also fights the loop's own FOV management (sprint/ADS) since it mutates camera.fov directly and calls updateProjectionMatrix outside the frame's FOV pipeline. Currently latent: _cameraPunch has no callers (grep). _cameraDip (29729) is likewise dead.
findings.fix: If used, drive a kick via the existing per-frame FOV system (add to a P._fovKick that decays in the loop) instead of mutating camera.fov + setTimeout, so it composes with sprint/ADS FOV and can't creep. Otherwise delete _cameraPunch/_cameraDip (29719-29731) as dead.
findings.risk: If wiring, must integrate with whatever owns camera.fov in the loop to avoid two writers fighting. Deletion is zero-risk.

findings.title: _stableFps frame limiter and applyOperatorConfig are dead; applyOperator (38833) is the real operator-config path
findings.description: _stableFps(targetFps) (29122) is a frame-rate gate that is never called — the loop runs uncapped via setAnimationLoop. applyOperatorConfig() (29131) gives Havoc +1 grenade/+1 smoke, but the LIVE operator setup is applyOperator() at 38833 (called from all run-start paths 32582/32859/38548/38769/45177). applyOperatorConfig is a duplicate, partial, never-called version — competing-definition smell even though it can't fire.
findings.evidence: function _stableFps(targetFps){...} // grep => def only. function applyOperatorConfig(){if(op==='havoc'){P.grenades+=1;P.smokes+=1;}} // grep applyOperatorConfig => def only; live path is applyOperator() (38833).
findings.fix: Delete _stableFps (29120-29129) and applyOperatorConfig (29130-29141). Verify Havoc's +1 grenade/+1 smoke is actually applied inside the live applyOperator() at 38833; if it isn't, fold it there (don't keep two operator-config functions).
findings.risk: Confirm applyOperator() already grants Havoc's grenade/smoke bonus before deleting applyOperatorConfig, else the bonus silently disappears. Low risk.

findings.title: _flashHitMarker, _flashKillBeat, spawnVictoryFireworks, spawnRainParticles, spawnSnowParticles are all defined but never called (duplicate/inert feedback)
findings.description: Several player-feedback/particle helpers are orphaned: _flashHitMarker (29644) — the live hit marker uses the hm-/hs class system (22622-22627) + G.hitMarkTimer (43749), so this older direct-opacity version would conflict if wired; _flashKillBeat (29652) — kill-beat is driven inline at 26925/32443/36606/22858; spawnVictoryFireworks (29686), spawnRainParticles (29702), spawnSnowParticles (29711) have no callers. Rain/snow ambience and victory fireworks are finished-but-unwired atmosphere.
findings.evidence: grep _flashHitMarker/_flashKillBeat/spawnVictoryFireworks/spawnRainParticles/spawnSnowParticles => each returns only its own definition line.
findings.fix: Visible win: call spawnVictoryFireworks(P.pos) on campaign clear / boss-down victory screen, and emit spawnRainParticles() a few times per frame in outdoor buildings (yacht=7, dock=1) gated by a per-frame budget to add weather ambience. Delete _flashHitMarker (conflicts with live hitmarker) and _flashKillBeat (redundant). spawnRainParticles uses RH+WT (defined globals) so it is safe to call.
findings.risk: Rain/snow push into G.trails every frame — gate by CONFIG.visual.particleCap and a per-frame count or it leaks meshes/materials and tanks FPS. Fireworks at victory is one-shot, safe.

findings.title: Cluster of never-called helpers: _xpProgress, _hudPulseColor, _flashEnemyAlert, updatePlayerFlags, squadChoreography, _checkPerfectBuilding, _gen* texture generators
findings.description: Confirmed-orphan helpers (grep shows definition only, no callers): _xpProgress/_xpForLevel/XP_CURVE (29758-29771); _hudPulseColor (30007); _flashEnemyAlert (30017) — note it adds a setTimeout that restores visorM.emissive but is never triggered; updatePlayerFlags + PLAYER_FLAGS (29896-29912) — flags written here are read nowhere; squadChoreography (30027); _checkPerfectBuilding (30230); and the procedural texture generators _genGraffiti/_genTrashTexture/_genCarpetPattern/_genWoodGrain (30248-30333). These inflate the file and are prime candidates for the 'feature half-wired so it never triggers' risk. _genGraffiti also returns a raw canvas while the sibling _gen* return THREE.CanvasTexture — inconsistent contract if ever used.
findings.evidence: grep _xpProgress/_hudPulseColor/_flashEnemyAlert/updatePlayerFlags/squadChoreography/_checkPerfectBuilding/_genGraffiti/_genTrashTexture/_genCarpetPattern/_genWoodGrain => each only its own def line. _genGraffiti returns canvas; _genTrashTexture returns new THREE.CanvasTexture(canvas).
findings.fix: Triage: delete the purely-vestigial ones (_hudPulseColor, updatePlayerFlags/PLAYER_FLAGS, squadChoreography, _xpProgress/XP_CURVE if no level UI). For ones worth keeping, wire them: e.g. call _flashEnemyAlert(e) when an enemy first detects the player (alert state transition) for a visible visor pulse — a cheap AAA tell. If keeping _genGraffiti, make it return new THREE.CanvasTexture(canvas) to match siblings.
findings.risk: Verify no string/dynamic dispatch references these before deleting (none found). Wiring _flashEnemyAlert is low-risk and adds readable enemy-detection feedback.
